headline: Guidance Gaps and the Road to Ed-Fi Summit
thesis: With schools adopting AI faster than rules or evidence can keep up, this week's coverage asks who sets the guardrails and who proves the results.
summary: Fresh sources were hard to reach today, so coverage leans on recent and still-live items. The throughline is governance and proof for AI in schools: Brookings weighs whether AI's risks outweigh its benefits for students, EdSurge reports that many districts and teachers still lack clear guidance, and Inside Higher Ed tracks faculty doubts about student work authenticity. On the infrastructure side, the Ed-Fi Alliance Summit (Nov 9–11) and 1EdTech's November sessions on evidence, QTI and learn-to-work data keep interoperability in focus.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · NOVEMBER 4, 2026 · Direct site fetches were unavailable in this run; items come from search results and recent carry-overs, so few are dated today.
